new_scholarship.name: Johns Hopkins International Scholarships
new_scholarship.program_type: University need-based grant and merit scholarship for international undergraduates
new_scholarship.duration: Typically four years; need-based aid awarded in the first year renews automatically in later years
new_scholarship.deadline: Financial Aid Deadline: November 15, 2026 for Early Decision I; January 15, 2027 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision; March 15, 2027 for transfer. Updated dates are made public in August each year.
new_scholarship.application_period: 2027 entry cycle. Early Decision I application deadline 1 November 2026 with financial aid deadline 15 November 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision application deadline 2 January 2027 with financial aid deadline 15 January 2027; transfer application deadline 1 March 2027 with financial aid deadline 15 March 2027. The Application Deadlines & Requirements page states that updated dates are made public in August each year.
new_scholarship.application_method: Merit scholarships are automatic on admission: all applicants are automatically considered for merit scholarships when they apply, no separate application is required, and recipients are notified at the time of the admissions decision. Need-based aid requires a separate, mandatory step: the applicant must indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and submit both the International Student Certification of Finances (COF) and the CSS Profile by the financial aid deadline of the chosen plan. No separate application exists for international applicants beyond the standard admissions application.
new_scholarship.description: Johns Hopkins is need-aware for international students rather than need-blind, meaning a family's financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process. For admitted international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid, and Hopkins offers a small number of merit scholarships to international citizens each year, for which all applicants are automatically considered with no additional application. Aid must be requested as a first-year applicant, and Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International first-year applicants who are not U.S. citizens, permanent residents, eligible noncitizens or DACA/undocumented holders, and whose families can show a lower ability to pay. International transfer students are not eligible for Hopkins financial aid, so this applies only to first-year entry.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is open to applicants who are not U.S. citizens, permanent residents, eligible noncitizens or DACA/undocumented holders, including citizens of another country attending secondary school in the U.S. Aid is limited: about 10% of international students receive financial aid, and Hopkins awards only a small number of merit scholarships to international citizens each year. Aid must be requested as a first-year applicant; international students who do not apply for financial aid as first-year applicants can never apply for aid later, and international students cannot apply for financial aid after admissions decisions are released. Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students. International citizens are eligible for merit scholarships in all admissions plans and receive the same financial aid consideration in each.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Merit scholarships are based on academic and personal achievement both in and outside the classroom; all applicants are automatically considered when they apply, regardless of citizenship or ability to pay, and selected recipients are notified with the admissions decision. Need-based scholarships are based solely on a family's ability to pay for college. Because Hopkins is need-aware for international citizens, financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process itself. Applicants in all admissions plans receive the same consideration for financial aid. Hopkins publishes no numerical weighting for either component.
new_scholarship.notes: No per-recipient award amount is published on the pages read, so funding_amount is null rather than an invented figure. Hopkins publishes no TOEFL/IELTS/DET minimum on the pages read; testing is required but the score thresholds sit on a separate standardized testing page that was not read, so english_requirement is null. programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Typically four years of undergraduate study. A need-based award made in the first year renews automatically in subsequent years without reapplication; the Hodson Trust Scholarship is described as renewable and the Charles R. Westgate Scholarship in Engineering covers four years of tuition.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: For recipients, tuition is covered: Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans for international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, and publishes that families making up to $200,000 pay no tuition. fully_funded is nevertheless false because three limits remain. First, the award is need-based and selective: only about 10% of international students receive financial aid and merit scholarships to international citizens are a small number each year, so admission does not confer funding. Second, it meets demonstrated need rather than the full cost of attendance, so the family must still contribute what it can pay and the amount varies with need and can change year to year. Third, international students are ineligible for Title IV federal aid and state aid, so no federal or state grant can top up a shortfall, and work-study is a separate opportunity rather than part of this award.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants who are neither U.S. citizens nor permanent residents, eligible noncitizens, nor holders of DACA or undocumented status. Applicants holding an F-1, F-2, M-1, J-1, J-2, G-series, A-2/A-3, NATO, B-1/B-2, H-series, L-series or U visa, and who do not have DACA or undocumented status, are international applicants at Hopkins.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible for both need-based and merit scholarships, although Hopkins states both types of assistance are limited. Hopkins is need-aware for international students, meaning financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process, whereas it is need-blind for domestic applicants. For all international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid, and a small number of merit scholarships are awarded to international citizens each year. All international applicants must submit the Certification of Finances; those seeking aid must also submit the CSS Profile. Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students, and international students are ineligible for federal and state aid.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Merit scholarships are automatic on admission: every applicant is automatically considered for merit scholarships when applying, no separate application is required, and recipients are notified at the time of the admissions decision. Need-based aid requires a separate, mandatory financial aid step: the applicant must indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and submit the International Student Certification of Finances plus the CSS Profile (or the free JHU ISFAA alternative) by the financial aid deadline of the chosen admissions plan. There is no separate application for international applicants beyond the standard admissions application, and international students cannot apply for financial aid after admissions decisions are released.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide your admissions plan early: the financial aid deadline (15 November 2026 for ED I, 15 January 2027 for ED II and Regular Decision) is later than the admissions deadline, and both are hard cutoffs
Confirm you are classified as an international applicant, since that classification determines both the Certification of Finances requirement and need-aware review
Indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application in the first year if you may need any assistance during the degree, because there is no later route to aid
Submit the Certification of Finances through the applicant portal as soon as the admissions application is submitted, since the form is generated there and every international applicant needs it
Submit the CSS Profile by the plan's financial aid deadline, or start the free JHU ISFAA alternative and allow the stated 5 to 7 days of processing time
Plan for a budget review of your family's income, assets and unusual circumstances before the CSS Profile, since need-based aid is determined solely from what a family can pay
Do not count on federal aid: international students are ineligible for Title IV funds, Pell and FSEOG
Have your school counselor send the secondary school report and arrange two teacher evaluations from different subject teachers
Block out mid-February for the mid-year school report request that arrives by email
If applying Early Decision I or II, arrange parent/guardian and counselor signatures for the binding Early Decision Agreement well before the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing the financial aid deadline rather than the admissions deadline, which voids the aid application
Failing to submit the Certification of Finances, which leaves the application incomplete for every international applicant regardless of aid request
Not indicating an interest in financial aid in the first year, after which aid is never available
Attempting to apply for need-based aid after the admissions decision is released, which Hopkins does not permit
Relying on a nonexistent CSS fee waiver; Hopkins does not issue them for international applicants, so the free JHU ISFAA is the fallback
Expecting admission to bring funding: only about 10% of international students receive aid, and merit awards to international citizens are a small number each year
Assuming need-blind treatment; Hopkins is need-aware for international students, so financial circumstances affect the admissions process itself
Applying as a transfer student and expecting aid, which Hopkins does not offer to international transfers
Underestimating the aid cliff: need is recalculated annually, so a family income increase can reduce the award in a later year
Omitting a verified English translation with non-English school documents
estimated_uncovered_costs: The family's own assessed contribution, because the award meets demonstrated need rather than the full cost of attendance
Whatever sits outside the cost of attendance calculation and is therefore not covered, such as international airfare, visa and immigration fees, and travel home
Books, supplies and personal expenses not covered by demonstrated need
Private education loans for international transfer students, where most lenders require a U.S. citizen co-signer and Hopkins includes no loans in its offers
Any gap created by an increase in family income or assets in a later year, since the award amount is recalculated each year

research_notes.logo: Located from the live header markup on apply.jhu.edu. The primary header mark is an inline SVG inside the .header-logo anchor (classes header-logo-large and header-logo-small, plus a header-logo-large--white variant) and therefore has no fetchable file URL, so it could not be byte-probed. The root /favicon.ico and /apple-touch-icon.png returned HTTP 200 with image content types on HEAD but delivered 0 bytes on GET, so they were rejected as unusable. The rel=icon and rel=apple-touch-icon links in the document head resolve to official assets under /wp-content/uploads/2022/11/ on apply.jhu.edu; the un-suffixed original https://apply.jhu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/cropped-cropped-favicon-194x194-1.png was downloaded and confirmed to be HTTP 200, content-type image/png, 76224 bytes, 512x512 per the PNG IHDR chunk, with valid PNG magic bytes rather than HTML. It was then opened and visually inspected to satisfy the white-on-transparent rule: it is the dark navy Johns Hopkins shield with book and globe motif on a white background, so it is legible on a light card. Served by jhu.edu itself, so official_host is true with host_evidence same_registrable_domain. No aggregator, CDN, Wikimedia or social asset was used.
